title: TaskScope enforces StructuredTaskScope structure rules
requirement: Keep TaskScope migratable to StructuredTaskScope once it is final (StructuredTaskScope is preview in JDK 27 and in JDK 28 early access 28-ea+17; no structured-concurrency JEP was targeted to JDK 28 as of 2026-09-26); ADR-0012 RT-Q1; plan §20 RT-02
acceptance: fork() throws TaskScope.StructureViolationException when a declared ScopedValue is bound to a different value than at open, or has become bound since open
fork() under the bindings in force at open is allowed

Closing a scope while scopes opened after it on the same thread are open closes those inner scopes first (cancelling and awaiting their subtasks), then this scope, then throws StructureViolationException
knownLimitation: Final APIs cannot enumerate a thread's ScopedValue bindings, so changes to undeclared keys, and rebinding a declared key to the identical object, are not detected. StructuredTaskScope detects both. This is documented in the TaskScope Javadoc and conventions §2.

red.revision: 95ed659 plus the StructureViolationException type (no enforcement) and the five new tests
red.result: 3 rule tests failed: 'Expected StructureViolationException to be thrown, but nothing was thrown'. 2 guard tests (same bindings; proper nesting) passed, as intended.

green.change: A per-thread open-scope stack (internal ThreadLocal, owner bookkeeping only); fork() compares declared keys with the bindings captured at open by identity; close() closes still-open inner scopes innermost first, then itself, then throws StructureViolationException with inner and own close failures suppressed. Class Javadoc documents the structure rules, their limitation and a part-by-part migration mapping to StructuredTaskScope.

refactor: Removed two unreachable defensive branches found by coverage (the scope-not-on-stack fallback and a CLOSED check in closeWithinStructure); the stack lookup is now a branch-free sublist. Conventions document v1.1 adds the structure rules, a migration section and a test-standard rule on interrupt races; plan §6.1 and the Copilot instructions link to the renumbered §6.

processDeviation.description: Behaviour implemented during green without a preceding failing test is covered by tests classified as retrospective characterization.
processDeviation.testDefectFound: The RT-02b test ownerInterruptedWhileCloseWaitsKeepsWaitingAndRestoresTheInterrupt was non-deterministic. It interrupted the owner from another thread and then released the subtask, and a virtual thread may observe termination before its own interrupt, so the interrupted wait path was sometimes not exercised although the test passed (seen as uncovered lines in one full verify; covered in 4 of 4 isolated runs). The owner now sets its own interrupt status before close(), making the path deterministic.

regression.result: 1,556 tests, 0 failures; JaCoCo gate met. TaskScope 163/163 lines and 70/70 branches; SubtaskImpl 63/64 lines and 17/18 branches (the documented start-of-run race guard)

sensitiveDataCheck: Logs contain Maven and test output only; no request bodies, credentials, keys or sensitive payloads.
